name: pumi-file-tree
description: The project tree in the sidebar: folders and files with their icons and git's marks, to open, rename, move, trash and search.

images.alt: The file tree in the sidebar, with file icons and git's marks, beside the file it opened

hide_gitignore.label: Hide ignored files
hide_gitignore.desc: Leave out of the tree what a .gitignore hides.

hide_hidden.label: Hide dotfiles
hide_hidden.desc: Leave out of the tree what starts with a dot.

file_icons.label: File icons
file_icons.desc: Draw each file's icon, by its name and its extension.

folder_icons.label: Folder icons
folder_icons.desc: Draw each folder's icon, open or closed.

git_status.label: Mark git's changes
git_status.desc: Tint a row by what git says of it, and by what is under it.

auto_fold_dirs.label: Fold single-child folders
auto_fold_dirs.desc: Draw a folder that holds one folder as one row, `a/b/c`, which opens a level at a time.

indent_size.label: Indent
indent_size.desc: How far one level of the tree is indented.

labels: A view of its own (the one showing it already, if any)
A tab on the right, drawn by the viewer that fits it
Your editor, in a terminal tab
open_with.label: Open a file with
open_with.desc: What a click on a file does: a new view holding the file (the view that shows it already comes forward instead), a tab on the right, a terminal tab running your editor, or whatever app owns it. A file's tab is drawn by the enabled viewer that fits it, such as the Code Editor.

editor.label: Editor
editor.desc: The editor a file opens in when `open_with` is your editor: `code -w`, `nvim`, `hx`. Empty is `$EDITOR`, and `vi` when that is empty too.

commands.title: File Tree: show the project tree
File Tree: reveal the current file in the tree
